mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pseudin-2, P2-LZ1, P2-LZ2, and P2-LZ4 have direct membrane-disruptive evidence in C. tropicalis or fungus-mimic membranes; P2-LZ3 is weaker and P2-LZ5 is not treated as a strong membranolytic analog.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: pseudin-2 and P2-LZ derivatives in C. tropicalis / model membranes
mechanism_claims.limitations: The claim is peptide-specific; P2-LZ5 is separated because the paper reports weaker membrane permeability and a different intracellular/mitochondrial pattern.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P2-LZ5 is source-supported as having a distinct intracellular/mitochondrial ROS-associated antifungal mechanism in C. tropicalis.
direct_assay_types: MitoSOX Red mitochondrial superoxide flow-cytometry/fluorescence assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source proposes mitochondrial membrane interaction and ROS generation; this is not generalized to all P2-LZ peptides.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: P2-LZ4 has source-supported in vivo antifungal efficacy in a C. tropicalis-infected mouse skin model; this is an efficacy claim, not a separate molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: P2-LZ4 and pseudin-2 in C. tropicalis mouse skin infection model
mechanism_claims.limitations: Kept distinct from direct mechanistic membrane/ROS claims.
